Well yes but actually no Validator set is closed So technically it is i guess yeah, I mean in practice it's PoS I guess now so I mean it is PoS but with PoA properties But validator set is closed so it actually is PoA Well, that is an interesting question Well it is PoS as you still need to stake sepolia and goerli are meant to be different use cases. sepolia for those that want to test execution (_i.e._ smart contracts) with a (supposedly) cleanly finalizing chain, and goerli for those who want to test consensus (_i.e._ validators). Yea, users can't run validators on Sepolia, which is fine as Sepolia is meant to be a "stable" testnet. but this means that this suggestion is still incomplete We still need goerli, or something that looks very like goerli. It may be easier to start a new chain at this stage, given that an ISC is work for client teams to handle. Yea it is. When there is no consensus for a irregular state change on goerli we'll need a new testnet with enough supply to test validator setups. I'd prefer not killing goerli immediately, as it's quite valuable to have a network that has popular dapps deployed on it. At least Nimbus explicitly documents using Goerli to test one's CL client setup before trying on mainnet, for example, yeah: https://nimbus.guide/prater.html Just would be great to discuss this.. The current situation is really annoying for many users. And it really doesn't need to be. Gathering GoETH is getting more complex than the whole validator setup procedure 😅 one valuable property is that it has approximately the same number of validators (well, within a smallish factor) as mainnet We can start a new testnet with as many validators as we want, so that wouldn't be an issue. Distribution of said validators is much better on goerli (prater) though, as lots of people have set up on it over time. On the flipside, participation is a bit lower because same people end up abandoning their testnet setups at some stage. The issue with starting a new testnet from scratch is finding people to run it reliably. Client teams already have enough on their plate and running another testnet the size of prater is both economically and logistically unfeasible. Deprecating goerli would take too long, a lot of orgs just moved to goerli now after ropsten was deprecated. It'd be unfair to ask them to move again so quickly, besides it'll take a while for the ecosystem (rpc, explorers, etc) to catch up. We can launch a new beaconchain on sepolia for e.g, one that isn't permissioned. But if we have x stakers join in and abandon their setup soon after, we'll quickly have an unusable setup. The solutions would have to be on the lines of: guaranteed exiting or somehow performing a re-genesis every few months. I guess going back to https://github.com/eth-clients/goerli/issues/97 and seeing how we can inflate the supply might be the easiest path forward :/ Hmm, what about a testnet with a much higher ejection balance? Something like 31ETH, so inactive validators get leaked out much faster. hmm, yea or even something higher could potentially mitigate the problem if we go with a fresh testnet. we'd have to make sure its token gated or something to avoid wasting the native supply. <@144468805697929216> other sepolia nodes are stuck syncing in a way they're not recovering from; that might need code fixes, not sure yet I don't think that starting a new testnet that's broadly equivalent to goerli would be a terrible thing, and inflating the Ether supply on goerli wouldn't come without its own issues. Not least it would be easy to grief consensus by starting up and abandoning lots of validators if Ether is plentiful. <@144468805697929216> it was a Nimbus bug, should be fixed by https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/pull/4161 so those nodes can recover > Not least it would be easy to grief consensus by starting up and abandoning lots of validators if Ether is plentiful. That's a _really_ good point. PoS doesn't work so well when what's being staked is worthless. 🙂 I like the idea of inflating goerli supply because we do need somewhere for people to register validators and test. In terms of the griefing it’s not a bad thing to have a testnet that regularly has long periods of non finality. And it would force us to make the social layer slashing simple to do so we could periodically remove offline validators. May need a hard fork to increase the ejection limit which is unfortunately hard to do because for some reason config values are immutable so we’d actually have to change code now rather than just updating the config at a specific epoch. Actually, how much supply do we actually need on goerli? IIRC Afri gave each of us validators 10M GoETH, if we pooled all that behind a couple faucets would that be enough? 12M goeth is enough to double the current validator set of 380k, how many validators do we actually _want_ on goerli? The problem isn't that there isn't enough for validators, it's that bots keep draining all the faucets and hording goeth. The aim is to have so much goeth that everyone realises it's worthless and bots can have relatively minimal restrictions without always running out. It is a good lesson that if we ever launch other testnets we should use the erc-20 version of the deposit contract with a token that we can arbitrarily mint more of so supply is never limited.

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
The issue with starting a new testnet from scratch is finding people to run it reliably. Client teams already have enough on their plate and running another testnet the size of prater is both economically and logistically unfeasible. Deprecating goerli would take too long, a lot of orgs just moved to goerli now after ropsten was deprecated. It'd be unfair to ask them to move again so quickly, besides it'll take a while for the ecosystem (rpc, explorers, etc) to catch up. 

We can launch a new beaconchain on sepolia for e.g, one that isn't permissioned. But if we have x stakers join in and abandon their setup soon after, we'll quickly have an unusable setup. The solutions would have to be on the lines of: guaranteed exiting or somehow performing a re-genesis every few months. 

I guess going back to https://github.com/eth-clients/goerli/issues/97 and seeing how we can inflate the supply might be the easiest path forward :/
